sections.h2: How the lake affects selling a house in St. Clair Shores
sections.html:
Lake St. Clair touches nearly every part of a St. Clair Shores sale, from canal and lakefront houses to the flood-zone check that follows insurance quotes. Water covers close to 19 percent of the city, and part of the city lies in the FEMA floodplain, so learn your own address's status early.

The city sits in southern Macomb County on the lake's western shore, about 14 miles northeast of downtown Detroit, and has 57,872 residents as of July 2025. Three selling routes are common:

  • A listing with an agent fits a well-kept house and an owner willing to wait out a buyer's loan.
  • A sale by owner saves the commission and leaves contracts and title steps to you.
  • A cash sale as-is suits deferred repairs, tenants or an estate. Compare offers and note who covers which closing costs, who handles the deed and when you get paid.

The city measures 14.40 square miles overall, with 2.72 of them water. About 14 miles of canals run mostly along the Nautical Mile, the Jefferson Avenue strip between 9 Mile and 10 Mile Roads that holds restaurants, boat dealers and marinas. Many subdivisions were platted early but built out after World War II, so older housing is common. Interstate 94 skirts the western edge through exits 224 to 230.

Population peaked decades ago: 63,096 residents in 2000, 59,715 in 2010 and 58,874 in 2020. Buyers see a settled lakeside community, so a clean, well-documented house and a clear flood status are what set a listing apart. Gather your survey, any insurance paperwork that mentions the flood zone and your permit records into one folder before the first showing, so a buyer's questions get quick, documented answers.

Neighbors matter when you describe a location. Roseville and Eastpointe lie to the west, and Harper Woods, Grosse Pointe Woods and Grosse Pointe Shores lie to the south across the Wayne County line. The area was part of Erin Township from 1843 to 1911 and then of Lake Township, so older records may carry those names. Ask the title company to search under them if a document looks incomplete.

FEMA redraws its maps now and then, so a parcel once in the floodplain may now be outside it, and the reverse can happen. Buyers often ask about flood status, since insurers and lenders look at it.

The city names two lookup tools:

  • Macomb County GIS: type the address, open Layers, expand Natural Features and tick Flood Zones. A parcel that turns red may be in the zone.
  • FEMA's flood map search by street address.

If an insurer has placed the house in the floodplain and you hold a survey or other evidence against it, you may qualify for a Letter of Map Amendment, or you can use the city's Options to Appeal Determination form. Sorting this out before listing spares you a surprise during a buyer's loan review.

sections.h2: Which school districts do buyers ask about?
sections.html:
Three public districts share the city. South Lake Schools covers the south, Lakeview Public Schools the middle and Lake Shore Public Schools the north, and each runs a high school inside the city limits. Ask the districts to confirm a specific address, because buyers want that detail.

Private options include St. Isaac Jogues and St. Joan of Arc, while St. Germaine closed in 2024. I-94 and Jefferson Avenue carry most commuters, and the average trip to work is 26.7 minutes.

The city wants every non-owner-occupied house registered and holding a certificate of approval before anyone moves in. Its registration form prints these terms:

  • Single-family house: $150 for the first 3,000 square feet, then $10 for each added 1,000 square feet.
  • Multiple-family building: $150 for the first unit, then $50 for each added unit in that building.
  • The fee pays for the first inspection and one follow-up. A rescheduled visit when nobody is on site costs $30, and a failed-compliance reinspection costs half the original fee.
  • An owner who lives beyond Wayne, Oakland, Macomb, Washtenaw and St. Clair counties must name a local agent.
  • Once the house sells, send the city a recorded deed or land contract to be dropped from its records.

Community Development and Inspections, at 586-447-3340, can confirm what applies to your address and whether an open permit needs closing before a sale.

sections.h2: Recording fees at the Macomb County Register of Deeds
sections.html:
The Register of Deeds in Mount Clemens, on N. Main Street, records deeds for a $30 fee however many pages they run. Of that amount, $4 supports the state survey and remonumentation fund. Call (586) 469-7953 with questions.

A tax certificate from the County Treasurer must come first for warranty deeds and land contracts, along with their covenant-clause and assignment variants. It costs $5 for up to five legal descriptions.

The county's transfer tax table multiplies the sale price by 0.0075 for the state and by 0.0011 for the county. Your title company can turn those rates into a dollar total at your price.

After closing, the buyer reports the change of ownership to the assessor on Form 2766 inside 45 days.

sections.h2: A simple order of steps for a quick sale
sections.html:
Start by checking your address in the flood tools, so you know the answer before a buyer asks. Print the result and keep it with your other sale papers. If the house is rented, confirm the registration and certificate of approval are current, and call Community Development and Inspections about any open permit. Then collect offers, and for each one note the price, the closing date and who pays which closing costs.

Once you accept, ask the title company to order the tax certificate if the deed is a warranty deed, confirm the transfer tax at your actual price, and record the deed in Mount Clemens. A cash buyer skips the lender's appraisal and loan review, which removes one common reason a closing slips, and lets you set the closing date in the contract, but the flood, rental and recording steps above still apply.

faqs.q: Is my St. Clair Shores house in a flood zone?
faqs.a: Check Macomb County GIS or FEMA's flood map search, both linked by the city. Part of the city is in the FEMA floodplain, and a survey that shows otherwise may support a Letter of Map Amendment.

faqs.q: What do recording and transfer tax cost on a Macomb sale?
faqs.a: Recording is $30 per document. The county schedule lists state transfer tax at 0.0075 of the sale price and county tax at 0.0011.

faqs.q: Do rental houses have to be registered in St. Clair Shores?
faqs.a: Yes. Registration and a certificate of approval come before occupancy, and a single-family house starts at $150 for the first 3,000 square feet.

faqs.q: Which school district serves my street?
faqs.a: South Lake Schools serves the south, Lakeview Public Schools the middle and Lake Shore Public Schools the north. Confirm your address with the district.
St. Clair Shores covers 14.40 square miles in total, with 2.72 of water, and the 2020 count was 58,874 residents.
